answer.rationale: The two declining metrics are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), so the highest-leverage single slot is one that acts directly on the funnel stage that is decaying rather than one that buys volume. memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value) is the closest match to the observed regression, with memory_31 (signup field reduction lifted SMB activation) as convergent prior evidence; memory_91 (in-product activation messaging) is the main rival and is why I spend my second verification pull there rather than elsewhere. I want the archived records for memory_86 and memory_91 specifically to check whether their lifts were measured on completion/engagement proxies only or carried through to retained qualified revenue, and whether the baseline funnel resembles today's post-decline funnel — a lift measured on a healthier funnel may not transfer. Promotional pricing is the tempting response to the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 is explicit that the 40% discount bought 31% signups and 18% revenue at the cost of 12 points of monthly retention on an unchanged segment definition; against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue that is a negative-value trade, and matching a price-led attack likely concedes the frame. Referral incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not touch the failing stage. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is sound but addresses a segment that is not the source of the decline. Key downstream risk I am flagging rather than assuming away: stripping onboarding and signup steps can remove the qualification and firmographic signal that feeds the sales-assisted enterprise path in memory_44, so a completion-rate win could quietly degrade pipeline quality and blended lead value. I therefore want the experiment instrumented on retained activation and downstream qualified-pipeline quality, not completion rate alone, and run as a standard controlled experiment with a holdout rather than a broad rollout, since memory_86 and memory_31 are consolidated summaries whose revenue-level durability is not yet established.
